connections.label: Roswell Incident
connections.note: TIER 3, CONTESTED. The Plains of San Agustin entered the Roswell corpus through Grady 'Barney' Barnett's reported account, transmitted second-hand and published in Berlitz and Moore's 'The Roswell Incident' (1980). The Air Force's own 1995 records review corroborates the route the story travelled - it records that in 1978 'a UFO researcher, Stanton Friedman, met with Marcel and began investigating', and that Moore and Berlitz 'reported they interviewed a number of persons who claimed to have been present at Roswell in 1947 and professed to be either firsthand or secondhand witnesses'. It does not corroborate the site: 'San Agustin', 'Barnett' and 'Maltais' each appear zero times in the entire report. Kevin Randle, named in that review among the researchers, concludes on the evidence: 'It is for these reasons, that is the lack of first-hand corroboration of the Barnett tale, the inability of the first people to talk of what Barnett said to provide a location and date and that the only source of the information is Barnett that I say, with confidence, that nothing happened there in July 1947.' Roswell is July 1947, so that conclusion severs the link by dating rather than by geography.

desc: The Plains of San Agustin is a large high-desert basin west of Socorro, New Mexico, best known today as the site of the Very Large Array. On this board it is the alleged second Roswell-adjacent recovery site, entering the record through Grady 'Barney' Barnett's reported account of coming upon a disc and bodies in July 1947, and later through Gerald Anderson's claimed childhood witness testimony. Both accounts are second-hand or contested in their provenance and neither is supported by a primary document; the site is retained because the Barnett account is one of the oldest strands in the Roswell corpus and its chain of transmission is itself a research object. GAO's 1995 records search found no surviving Roswell AAF message traffic that would corroborate or refute activity here.
